category: Porous Media Flow and Subsurface Flow Modules: Darcy, Richards, Fracture, Two-Phase and Multiphase Porous Flow, Poroelasticity
description: Interfaces, features and multiphysics couplings of the COMSOL Porous Media Flow and Subsurface Flow Modules (also partly in CFD, Microfluidics and others): Darcy's Law domain/boundary/edge features, permeability, storage and retention models, Richards' equation, dual porosity/permeability, fracture and layered flow, two-phase Darcy, multiphase flow in porous media with wells, free-porous coupling, Brinkman–Forchheimer and poroelasticity, with verified Java type strings and variables (COMSOL 6.4).

tools.name: Richards' Equation (dl)
tools.description: Interface for variably saturated flow in porous media (vadose zone, soil infiltration, drainage, wicking): Richards' equation with van Genuchten, Brooks–Corey or user-defined retention and relative permeability relations, so hydraulic properties change as pores fill and drain. Default nodes are Unsaturated Porous Medium, No Flow and Initial Values; stationary and time-dependent analyses.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Porous Media and Subsurface Flow > Richards' Equation (dl); Java: physics().create("dl", "PorousMediaFlowRichards", "geom1")

parameters.name: Unsaturated Porous Medium
parameters.description: Storage model and Fluid/Porous Matrix subnodes with retention model.

parameters.name: Gravity
parameters.description: Elevation D (default z/y) for hydraulic and pressure head.

parameters.name: Boundary conditions
parameters.description: Pressure head, Hydraulic head, Precipitation, Atmosphere/Gauge, Mass Flux, Pervious Layer.

tools.notes: Requires the Porous Media Flow or Subsurface Flow Module. Java id PorousMediaFlowRichards (RichardsEquation is the backward-compatible id). Default tag is dl, like Darcy's Law.

tools.name: Fracture Flow (ff)
tools.description: Interface for flow along faults and fractures represented as interior or exterior boundaries in 3D (edges in 2D), using a tangential Darcy's law integrated over the fracture aperture. It models highly conductive fracture networks in rock, fissured aquifers and thin porous layers without meshing their thickness; combine with Darcy's Law for matrix flow.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Porous Media and Subsurface Flow > Fracture Flow (ff); Java: physics().create("ff", "PorousMediaFlowFracture", "geom1")

parameters.name: Fracture node
parameters.description: Fluid (Fracture) and Fracture Material subnodes (aperture, permeability, porosity).

parameters.name: Edge/point conditions
parameters.description: Pressure, heads, Mass Flux, Inlet, Outlet at fracture edges.

tools.notes: Java id PorousMediaFlowFracture with default tag ff; the older FractureFlow id (tag esff) is kept for backward compatibility. Only highly conductive fractures; use the Darcy's Law Fracture feature for coupled matrix–fracture flow.

tools.name: Layered Darcy's Law (ldl)
tools.description: 3D boundary interface for flow within thin layered porous materials (composites, paper, geotextiles, membranes) defined as layered materials on surfaces: a Darcy's law variant on the product space of the surface and an extra through-thickness dimension, so pressure variation across the layers is resolved without meshing the thickness. Different layers can have different properties.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Porous Media and Subsurface Flow > Layered Darcy's Law (ldl); Java: physics().create("ldl", "LayeredDarcysLaw", "geom1")

parameters.name: Layered material
parameters.description: Single Layer Material, Layered Material Link/Stack or Material with layer thickness.

parameters.name: Interface features
parameters.description: Pressure/Mass Flux/Inlet/Outlet/Thin Barrier, Interface variants on layer interfaces.

tools.notes: Requires the Porous Media Flow Module; 3D only. Combine with Layered Shell for poroelastic layered structures.

tools.name: Two-Phase Darcy's Law (tpdl)
tools.description: Interface solving Darcy's law for the total (average) pressure plus a transport equation for the fluid content (saturation) of one of two immiscible fluids, including relative permeabilities and capillary pressure or capillary diffusion. It suits water–oil displacement, gas–water flow in soils and CO2 injection at moderate complexity.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Porous Media and Subsurface Flow > Two-Phase Darcy's Law (tpdl); Java: physics().create("tpdl", "TwoPhaseDarcysLaw", "geom1")

parameters.name: Fluids and Matrix Properties
parameters.description: Densities, viscosities, relative permeabilities, porosity, permeability and capillary model.

parameters.name: Dependent variables
parameters.description: Pressure and fluid content (saturation) of fluid 1.

parameters.name: Boundary nodes
parameters.description: No Flux (default), Pressure and Saturation, Mass Flux, Inlet, Outlet, Thin Barrier, Well.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD or Subsurface Flow Module. For more than two phases or wells use Multiphase Flow in Porous Media.

tools.name: Multiphase Flow in Porous Media (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined interface combining Darcy's Law (total flow) with Phase Transport in Porous Media (saturations of any number of immiscible phases) through the Multiphase Flow in Porous Media coupling. It handles capillary pressure, relative permeabilities, gravity segregation and wells, for reservoir engineering, CO2 storage, NAPL contamination and wicking.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Porous Media and Subsurface Flow > Multiphase Flow in Porous Media

parameters.name: Phases
parameters.description: Defined in Phase Transport; one from the volume constraint.

tools.notes: Available with CFD, Porous Media Flow, Subsurface Flow or Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer Modules.

tools.name: Multiphase Flow in Porous Media (Multiphysics Coupling)
tools.description: Domain coupling (default name mfpm1) that bidirectionally links Phase Transport in Porous Media and Darcy's Law: the phase saturations determine total mobility and density used by Darcy's law, and the Darcy velocity and pressure drive the phase transport including capillary and gravity contributions.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Multiphase Flow in Porous Media; Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("mfpm1", "MultiphaseFlowInPorousMedia", 3)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Phase transport and Flow in porous media.

tools.notes: Verified type string MultiphaseFlowInPorousMedia.

tools.name: Well (Multiphase Flow in Porous Media Coupling)
tools.description: Optional multiphysics coupling on points (2D) or edges (3D) that represents injection or production wells in multiphase porous flow, bidirectionally linking Phase Transport in Porous Media and Darcy's Law. The total mass flow rate, rate per length or bottom-hole conditions are given, and injected phase fractions are specified for injection wells.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Well (edges in 3D, points in 2D) under a Multiphase Flow in Porous Media setup (default name wellmpp1)

parameters.name: Total mass flow rate M0 / per unit length

tools.example:
// GUI: Multiphysics > right-click > Well; select the horizontal well edges; Injection, Total mass flow rate = 5[kg/s], injected CO2 fraction = 1
// Application Library: Subsurface_Flow_Module/Fluid_Flow/reservoir_horizontal_wells, carbon_dioxide_storage
tools.notes: Requires the Subsurface Flow Module license.

tools.name: Free and Porous Media Flow, Darcy (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined interface coupling Laminar Flow in free-flow domains with Darcy's Law in porous domains through the Free and Porous Media Flow Coupling on their shared boundaries. It is the efficient alternative to the Brinkman-based Free and Porous Media Flow interface when flow inside the porous medium is slow and Darcian (filters, membranes, reverse osmosis modules).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Porous Media and Subsurface Flow > Free and Porous Media Flow, Darcy

parameters.name: Domain selection
parameters.description: Laminar Flow on free domains, Darcy's Law on porous domains.

tools.notes: Available with CFD, Porous Media Flow, Subsurface Flow and Microfluidics Modules.

tools.name: Free and Porous Media Flow Coupling (Multiphysics Coupling)
tools.description: Boundary coupling (default name nsd1) between Laminar Flow and Darcy's Law: continuity of normal mass flux and of normal stress/pressure across the free–porous interface, with an optional Beavers–Joseph slip condition for the tangential velocity on the free-flow side. The selection defaults to the boundaries shared by both interfaces.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Free and Porous Media Flow Coupling; Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("nsd1", "NavierStokesDarcyCoupling", 2)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Free flow (spf) and Porous media flow (dl).

parameters.name: Beavers–Joseph slip
parameters.description: Tangential slip with a dimensionless slip coefficient.

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: Interface boundaries between free and porous domains.

tools.notes: Verified type string NavierStokesDarcyCoupling (GUI name: Free and Porous Media Flow Coupling).

tools.name: Poroelasticity (Multiphysics Coupling)
tools.description: Domain coupling (default name poro1) used by the Poroelasticity, Solid interface (Porous Media Flow, Subsurface Flow, Geomechanics or Structural Mechanics Modules) that links Solid Mechanics and Darcy's Law bidirectionally following Biot theory: effective stress uses the pore pressure times the Biot–Willis coefficient, and the porosity/storage change is driven by the volumetric strain rate. It handles geometrically linear and nonlinear (large strain) poroelasticity consistently with the solid material settings, for consolidation, soft tissues, hydrogels and reservoir compaction.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Poroelasticity; Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("poro1", "PoroelasticCoupling", 3)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Solid mechanics and Flow in porous media.

parameters.name: Large strain
parameters.description: Follows the Formulation setting of the solid material model.

tools.notes: Verified in COMSOL 6.4: the working type string is PoroelasticCoupling (the GUI label is Poroelasticity).

tools.name: Two-Phase Flow, Level Set, Brinkman Equations (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined interface coupling the Brinkman Equations with a Level Set interface and the Two-Phase Flow, Level Set coupling (plus optional Wetted Wall) to track a resin/air front moving through a porous preform, for example resin transfer molding and impregnation. Capillary effects inside the pores are neglected, which is valid at high filling velocities.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Two-Phase Flow, Level Set > Two-Phase Flow, Level Set, Brinkman Equations
tools.notes: For capillary-dominated porous two-phase flow use Multiphase Flow in Porous Media.

tools.name: Porous Medium (Darcy's Law): Flow and Storage Models
tools.description: Default domain node of Darcy's Law adding continuity with the Darcy velocity. The flow model is Darcian (linear) or non-Darcian (Forchheimer-type quadratic resistance), and the storage model defines the transient term: from density and porosity, linearized storage, poroelastic storage, quasistatic (no storage) or a user-defined storage coefficient. Fluid and Porous Matrix subnodes hold fluid and matrix properties.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Porous Medium (porous1); Java: physics("dl").feature("porous1").set("storageModelType", "linearized")

parameters.name: permeabilityModelType
parameters.description: permeability | conductivity | kozenyCarman | powerLaw | klinkenberg | forchheimer | ergun | burkePlummer | userdef.

tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4. Java id of Darcy's Law is PorousMediaFlowDarcy (DarcysLaw is the backward-compatible id).

tools.name: Porous Matrix (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Subnode of Porous Medium/Unsaturated Porous Medium defining porosity ε_p (usually from a Porous Material), the effective matrix compressibility for storage, and the permeability model: permeability κ (isotropic, diagonal or symmetric tensor), hydraulic conductivity K, Kozeny–Carman from particle diameter or a porosity power law; for non-Darcian flow Forchheimer, Ergun, Burke–Plummer, Klinkenberg (gas slippage) or user-defined inertial resistance.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Porous Medium > Porous Matrix (pm1); Java: physics("dl").feature("porous1").feature("pm1").set("kappa", ...)

parameters.name: dp / cf / bk / bPL, nPL
parameters.description: Particle diameter, Forchheimer parameter (0.55), Klinkenberg parameter, power-law constants.

tools.notes: Property names verified by a solved COMSOL 6.4 probe model.

tools.name: Permeability Models: Kozeny–Carman, Ergun, Forchheimer, Burke–Plummer, Klinkenberg
tools.description: Constitutive relations for the capacity of a porous medium to transmit flow: Kozeny–Carman estimates κ from porosity and mean particle diameter for packed beds and granular soils; Ergun adds a quadratic inertial term for Re > 10; Forchheimer adds an inertial drag with coefficient c_F; Burke–Plummer is the turbulent (inertia-only) limit; Klinkenberg corrects gas permeability for slip at low pressure (κ = κ∞(1 + b_K/p)).
tools.usage: Darcy's Law / Brinkman > Porous Medium > Porous Matrix > Permeability model (permeabilityModelType)

parameters.name: klinkenberg
parameters.description: κ∞ and Klinkenberg parameter b_K (default 1e3 Pa).

tools.notes: Non-Darcian options require flowModelType = nonDarcian; the Unsaturated Porous Medium allows only Darcian models.

tools.name: Fluid (Darcy's Law): Fluid Type and Compressibility
tools.description: Subnode of Porous Medium defining fluid density and dynamic viscosity (from material or user input), the fluid type (incompressible, compressible, linearized compressible with compressibility χ_f, ideal gas with gas constant or molar mass), optional inelastic non-Newtonian viscosity with an apparent-shear-rate correction and a thermal shift function.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Porous Medium > Fluid (fluid1); Java: physics("dl").feature("porous1").feature("fluid1").set("fluidType", "idealGas")
tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Darcy Velocity and Head Variables (dl.u, dl.U, dl.H, dl.Hp)
tools.description: Postprocessing variables of Darcy's Law (verified in COMSOL 6.4): Darcy (superficial) velocity components dl.u, dl.v, dl.w and magnitude dl.U, hydraulic head dl.H, pressure head dl.Hp, elevation dl.D, absolute pressure dl.pA, density dl.rho, viscosity dl.mu, porosity dl.epsilon, mass source dl.Qm and storage coefficient dl.Sp. The average linear (seepage) velocity equals the Darcy velocity divided by porosity.
tools.usage: Results > Expression, e.g. dl.U or dl.H; Java: model.result("pg1").feature("surf1").set("expr", "dl.H")

parameters.name: dl.H, dl.Hp, dl.D
parameters.description: Hydraulic head, pressure head and elevation (m).

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: Dependent variable pressure (gauge relative to the reference pressure).

tools.notes: Replace dl by the interface tag in use; dependent-variable name p may be renamed.

tools.name: Unsaturated Porous Medium (Richards' Equation)
tools.description: Domain node adding Richards' equation for variably saturated flow, with Fluid and Porous Matrix (retention model) subnodes. The storage term is derived from the retention model (specific moisture capacity), a linearized storage (default), liquid content, or user input; it is the default node of Richards' Equation and also available in Darcy's Law.
tools.usage: Richards' Equation > Unsaturated Porous Medium (usporous1); Java: physics("dl").feature("usporous1").set("storageModelType", "fromliquid")

parameters.name: retentionModel
parameters.description: vanGenuchten | BrooksAndCorey | userdef (set in Porous Matrix).

tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Retention Models: van Genuchten and Brooks–Corey (Richards' Equation)
tools.description: Constitutive relations giving effective saturation, liquid volume fraction, specific moisture capacity and relative permeability as functions of pressure head in unsaturated soils: van Genuchten (α, n, l, with m = 1 - 1/n), Brooks and Corey (air-entry head and pore size index), or fully user-defined expressions with residual liquid volume fraction θ_r.
tools.usage: Unsaturated Porous Medium > Porous Matrix > Retention Model

parameters.name: User defined
parameters.description: Se, θ_l, C_m and κ_r expressions.

tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Dual Porosity Medium (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Domain node for media with a flowing macropore (fracture) system and a storing micropore (matrix block) system that exchanges fluid with it through an interporosity transfer term α_w(p_M - p_m); only the macropores conduct flow. Typical for fractured rock and aggregated soils, with Fluid, Macropores and Micropores subnodes.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Dual Porosity/Permeability > Dual Porosity Medium; Java: physics("dl").create("dporo1", "DualPorosityMedium", 2)

parameters.name: Storage model
parameters.description: From density and porosity, linearized, poroelastic, quasistatic or user defined for macro and micro systems.

parameters.name: Macropores / Micropores
parameters.description: Porosity and permeability of each system.

tools.notes: Requires the Subsurface Flow or Porous Media Flow Module.

tools.name: Dual Permeability Medium and Unsaturated Dual Permeability Medium (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Domain nodes where both macropores and micropores conduct flow, each with its own Darcy (or Richards) equation coupled by an interporosity transfer; the unsaturated variant uses retention models in both systems. They model preferential flow in structured soils, irrigation infiltration and fractured-porous aquifers.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law / Richards' Equation > Dual Porosity/Permeability > Dual Permeability Medium / Unsaturated Dual Permeability Medium; Java ids DualPermeabilityMedium, UnsaturatedDualPermeabilityMedium

parameters.name: Macropores / Micropores
parameters.description: Porosity, permeability (and retention) of each system.

tools.notes: Two pressure fields are solved, roughly doubling the degrees of freedom.

tools.name: Mass Source (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Domain source Q_m (kg/(m³·s)) added to the Darcy's law continuity equation for distributed recharge, extraction, reactions producing gas, or coupling to other physics. In Fracture Flow it is multiplied by the fracture thickness.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Mass Source; Java: physics("dl").create("ms1", "MassSource", 2)
tools.notes: Evaluate dl.Qm to check the applied source.

tools.name: Line Mass Source and Point Mass Source (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Concentrated sources for Darcy's Law: a Line Mass Source (kg/(m·s)) on edges (3D) or points (2D) represents boreholes and drains, and a Point Mass Source (kg/s) represents injection points. They avoid meshing small well diameters in regional models.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Edges > Line Mass Source / Points > Point Mass Source; Java: physics("dl").create("lms1", "LineMassSource", 1); create("pms1", "PointMassSource", 0)
tools.notes: For wells with a specified pressure or head use the Well feature instead.

tools.name: Contributing Velocity (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Subnode that adds an extra velocity field u_ctrb to the Darcy velocity used in the continuity equation, for example regional background flow, osmotic or electroosmotic contributions, or velocities computed by other physics. Several contributions are additive and available as name.uctrb.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Porous Medium > Contributing Velocity; Java: physics("dl").feature("porous1").create("ctrv1", "ContributingVelocity", 2)

parameters.name: Contributing velocity u_ctrb
parameters.description: Vector field (user defined or from another interface).

parameters.name: Coordinate system
parameters.description: System in which the vector is given.

tools.notes: Available under Porous Medium, Unsaturated Porous Medium and Dual Porosity Medium.

tools.name: Cross Section and Thickness (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Nodes overriding the global out-of-plane geometry: Cross Section sets the cross-sectional area of 1D domains (columns, pipes of porous material) and Thickness sets the out-of-plane thickness of 2D domains, so fluxes and sources are scaled correctly in reduced-dimension models.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Cross Section (1D) / Thickness (2D); Java: physics("dl").create("cs1", "CrossSection", 1); create("th1", "Thickness", 2)
tools.notes: Global defaults are set in the interface Physical Model section.

tools.name: Pressure (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Dirichlet condition p = p0 on boundaries (and on edges in 3D with the Subsurface Flow Module), relative to the reference pressure. It is the usual condition at reservoirs, rivers and outlets with known pressure; can also be used on identity pairs and fracture edges.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Pressure; Java: physics("dl").create("pr1", "Pressure", 2); feature("pr1").set("p0", ...)
tools.notes: Verified in a solved COMSOL 6.4 probe.

tools.name: Pressure Head and Hydraulic Head (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Groundwater-style Dirichlet conditions: Pressure Head fixes H_p = p/(ρg) and Hydraulic Head fixes H = H_p + D (elevation), which is natural for aquifers with measured water levels, lakes and rivers. Both are available on boundaries, pairs and fracture edges.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Hydraulics > Pressure Head / Hydraulic Head; Java: physics("dl").create("hh1", "HydraulicHead", 2); create("ph1", "PressureHead", 2)

parameters.name: Gravity
parameters.description: Elevation D from the Gravity node.

tools.notes: Include gravity so that H and H_p differ by the elevation.

tools.name: Atmosphere/Gauge (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Boundary condition setting the pressure to atmospheric (p = 0 gauge), so the total hydraulic potential reduces to the gravitational potential; used at seepage faces, springs and free surfaces exposed to air.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Hydraulics > Atmosphere/Gauge; Java: physics("dl").create("ag1", "Atmosphere", 2)
tools.notes: Java type id is Atmosphere.

tools.name: Mass Flux (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Neumann condition prescribing the inward mass flux N0 through boundaries (positive into the domain), for recharge, pumping rates or measured infiltration. No Flow is the special case N0 = 0 and is the default on exterior boundaries.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Mass Flux; Java: physics("dl").create("mf1", "MassFlux", 2); feature("mf1").set("N0", ...)
tools.notes: For rain on inclined surfaces use Precipitation with slope correction.

tools.name: Inlet and Outlet (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Inlet prescribes normal inflow velocity (Darcy velocity U0), pressure or mass flow (mass flow rate, pointwise mass flux, standard flow rate or SCCM) on a boundary; Outlet provides the corresponding outflow conditions. They make porous flow setups consistent with free-flow interfaces.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Inlet / Outlet; Java: physics("dl").create("inl1", "Inlet", 2); feature("inl1").set("BoundaryCondition", "Velocity")
tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Flux Discontinuity (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Interior boundary condition prescribing a jump N0 in normal mass flux across an internal surface, for example leakage through a thin layer into a region not modeled or a distributed source on an interface.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Thin Structures > Flux Discontinuity; Java: physics("dl").create("fd1", "FluxDiscontinuity", 2)

parameters.name: N0
parameters.description: Flux discontinuity (positive opposite to the boundary normal).

tools.notes: Only on interior boundaries.

tools.name: Precipitation (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Boundary inflow condition for rainfall or irrigation given as a precipitation rate (e.g., mm/day) normal to the boundary, with optional slope correction for inclined ground surfaces. It is used in hydrogeology and slope infiltration models with Richards' equation.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law / Richards' Equation > Hydraulics > Precipitation; Java: physics("dl").create("prec1", "Precipitation", 2)
tools.notes: Rainfall exceeding infiltration capacity requires switching to a head condition (ponding) with events or logical expressions.

tools.name: Barrier (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Interior boundary condition representing a thin permeable wall, membrane, geotextile or clay layer with thickness d_b and permeability κ_b (scalar or tensor), so the pressure jumps across it according to its resistance. Avoids meshing thin low-permeability layers.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Thin Structures > Barrier; Java: physics("dl").create("tb1", "ThinBarrier", 2)
tools.notes: Java type id is ThinBarrier (GUI label Barrier).

tools.name: Pervious Layer (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Leakage (Robin) boundary condition for flux through a semi-pervious layer connected to an external water body at a given pressure, pressure head or hydraulic head: N = ρ R_b [(p_b - p)/(ρg) + D_b - D], with conductance R_b = K'/B' of the layer. It models aquitards, riverbeds and lake bottoms.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Hydraulics > Pervious Layer; Java: physics("dl").create("pl1", "PerviousLayer", 2)

parameters.name: Rb
parameters.description: Conductance (1/s) = hydraulic conductivity / thickness of the layer.

tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Well (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Edge (3D) or point (2D) feature modeling injection or production wells with a given well diameter and either bottom-hole pressure, pressure head, hydraulic head or mass flow (total, per unit length, or flux), without meshing the borehole. Used for groundwater pumping tests, geothermal doublets and aquifer storage.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Edges (3D) / Points (2D) > Well; Java: physics("dl").create("well1", "Well", 1)
tools.notes: Requires the Subsurface Flow Module. Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Fracture (Darcy's Law) and Fracture Material
tools.description: Boundary feature of Darcy's Law that adds tangential Darcy flow along interior boundaries representing fractures embedded in the porous matrix, coupled to the matrix pressure. Subnodes Fluid (Fracture) and Fracture Material define fluid properties and fracture aperture, permeability (or cubic law) and porosity; edges of fractures accept pressure, heads and mass flux conditions.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Fracture; Java: physics("dl").create("frac1", "Fracture", 2)

parameters.name: Permeability
parameters.description: From material, user defined or cubic law from aperture.

tools.notes: Heat and solute transport in fractures use the Heat Transfer in Fractures and Transport of Diluted Species in Fractures interfaces.

tools.name: Gravity and Elevation (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Default Gravity node of Darcy's Law and Richards' Equation that adds the body force ρg to Darcy's law and defines the elevation D used for hydraulic head, pressure head and hydrostatic boundary conditions. Gravity is essential for buoyancy-driven porous flow (saltwater intrusion, Elder problem) and unsaturated flow.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > Gravity (gr1); interface setting Include gravity
tools.example:
// GUI: Darcy's Law > Physical Model > Include gravity; Gravity 1 > Elevation D = z
// Application Library: Subsurface_Flow_Module/Solute_Transport/buoyancy_darcy_elder
tools.notes: Variable dl.D verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Fluid and Matrix Properties (Layered Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Default node of the Layered Darcy's Law interface adding Darcy's law in each layer with fluid properties (from the boundary material) and matrix porosity/permeability per layer; subnodes Richards' Equation Model, Storage Model and Poroelastic Storage define unsaturated behavior, storage and poroelastic coupling for layered media.
tools.usage: Layered Darcy's Law > Fluid and Matrix Properties (dlm1); add Richards' Equation Model (RichardsEquationModel), Storage Model (StorageModel) or Poroelastic Storage (PoroelasticMaterial)

parameters.name: Shell properties
parameters.description: Use all layers or select individual layers.

tools.notes: Type ids from the COMSOL 6.4 plugin registry.

tools.name: Fluids and Matrix Properties (Two-Phase Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Domain node of Two-Phase Darcy's Law with properties of both fluids (density, viscosity, relative permeability), matrix porosity and permeability, and the capillary model: capillary diffusion (tensor D_c) or capillary pressure from van Genuchten (entry pressure, m_vG, l_vG), Brooks–Corey (entry pressure, λ_p) or a user expression.
tools.usage: Two-Phase Darcy's Law > Fluids and Matrix Properties (fmp1); Java: physics("tpdl").feature("fmp1").set("capillarymodel", "Capillarypressure")

parameters.name: pressuremodel
parameters.description: vanGenuchten (pec, mvG, lvG) | BrooksCorey (pec, lambdap) | Userdefined (pc).

parameters.name: rho1, mu1, kappar1 / rho2, mu2, kappar2
parameters.description: Fluid 1 and 2 properties and relative permeabilities.

tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Pressure and Saturation (Two-Phase Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Boundary condition prescribing both pressure p and saturation of fluid 1 (s2 = 1 - s1) on a boundary, typically at injection faces or constant-pressure reservoirs in two-phase displacement problems.
tools.usage: Two-Phase Darcy's Law > Pressure and Saturation; Java: physics("tpdl").create("pas1", "PressureSaturation", 2)
tools.notes: Use Inlet (mass flux of each fluid) when rates instead of pressure are known.

tools.name: Porous Medium with Forchheimer Drag (Brinkman Equations)
tools.description: Domain node of the Brinkman Equations and Free and Porous Media Flow interfaces solving the Brinkman momentum equation (Darcy drag plus viscous shear and optional inertia) with Fluid and Porous Matrix subnodes; a Forchheimer drag term (β proportional to |u|) can be added for high pore Reynolds numbers. It suits packed beds, filters and fast flow through open-cell foams.
tools.usage: Brinkman Equations > Porous Medium (porous1) > Porous Matrix + Forchheimer drag; Java: physics().create("br", "PorousMediaFlowBrinkman", "geom1")
tools.notes: Java id PorousMediaFlowBrinkman (Brinkman is the backward-compatible id).

tools.name: Flownet Plot (Richards' Equation)
tools.description: Default plot generated for 2D and 2D axisymmetric Richards' Equation models combining streamlines of the Darcy velocity with contours of pressure (or head), giving the classical flow net used in groundwater engineering to assess seepage and gradients.
tools.usage: Generated automatically when solving Richards' Equation in 2D; Results > Flownet
tools.notes: Available in 2D and 2D axisymmetric components only.

tools.name: Permeability Estimation from Pore-Scale Flow (Porous Media Homogenization)
tools.description: Workflow to obtain macroscopic permeability and porosity of a porous material from its microstructure: solve Creeping Flow through a representative volume element (imported CT/CAD pore geometry or generated packing) with a small pressure drop, then compute κ = μ U_avg L / Δp from Darcy's law and ε from the pore volume fraction. The resulting values feed Darcy's Law or Brinkman models at the device scale.
tools.usage: Creeping Flow (spf) on the pore space + Pressure inlet/outlet + Symmetry/Periodic walls; Results: Global Evaluation of mean velocity and pressure drop

parameters.name: RVE size
parameters.description: Large enough that averaged quantities are representative.

parameters.name: Pressure drop Δp
parameters.description: Small enough to stay in the Darcian (creeping) regime.

parameters.name: Averaged superficial velocity
parameters.description: Flow rate divided by the total RVE cross section.

tools.notes: Directional permeabilities (tensor components) require separate runs with the pressure drop along each axis.

tools.name: No Flow, Interior Wall and Symmetry (Darcy's Law)
tools.description: Impermeable conditions of Darcy's Law: No Flow (default on exterior boundaries) sets zero normal Darcy flux, Interior Wall applies no flux on both sides of interior boundaries so thin impermeable sheets need not be meshed, and Symmetry imposes zero normal flux on symmetry planes. Periodic Condition is available for repeating structures.
tools.usage: Darcy's Law > No Flow (nf1, default) / Thin Structures > Interior Wall / Symmetry; Java: physics("dl").create("iw1", "InteriorWall", 2); create("sym1", "Symmetry", 2)

parameters.name: Interior Wall
parameters.description: Allows pressure discontinuity across the boundary.

tools.notes: Barrier (ThinBarrier) is the permeable counterpart of Interior Wall.

tools.name: Darcian and Non-Darcian Flow Regimes (Porous Media)
tools.description: Guideline for choosing the porous flow model: Darcy's linear law holds for pore Reynolds numbers Re < 10 (Kozeny–Carman), the transitional regime 10 < Re < 1000 needs a quadratic (Ergun/Forchheimer) term, and Re > 1000 approaches the Burke–Plummer turbulent limit; gas flow at high Knudsen number (Kn > 0.1) needs slip corrections such as Klinkenberg. Brinkman equations add viscous shear for high-porosity media and free–porous transitions.
tools.usage: Reference (Porous Media Flow Module User's Guide > About Darcian and Non-Darcian Flow); select Porous Medium > Flow model: Darcian or Non-Darcian

parameters.name: Re (bed)
parameters.description: ρ U d_p / μ based on superficial velocity and particle diameter.

parameters.name: Kn
parameters.description: Mean free path over pore size.

tools.notes: Evaluate the bed Reynolds number from dl.U after a first Darcian solution to check validity.
